# Legal facts the app is still waiting on

The customer app ships four legal pages: Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, Refund & Cancellation
Policy, and Grievance Redressal. They are reachable in the app (Profile → More, plus terms and
privacy on the sign-in screen) and published as static HTML at `/legal/<slug>` on the Customer
app's own hosting — not `burgonomics.com`, which is out of scope for this wave — so a store
listing can point at a real URL.

Two things must be true before those pages go to a store:

1. **No page may still show a `[TO BE SUPPLIED: …]` mark.** Those marks are facts only the owner
   can supply, listed below as **M1-M4**. While any mark is on a page,
   the page itself says so in a banner and **the release checklist blocks**.
2. **Every fact printed but never verified must be confirmed** — listed below as
   **C1-C3**. Those print as ordinary values, so a wrong one is
   silent, which is exactly why they block the release too.

Both lists are generated from
`burgonomics-foundation-core/src/features/legal/content/legalContent.ts`
(`LEGAL_PLACEHOLDERS` and `LEGAL_FACTS_TO_CONFIRM`), the same module that renders the pages, so
the copy a customer reads and the list the owner works from cannot drift apart.

**Status today: 4 facts missing, 3 facts unverified.**
This is not a prediction: the pages currently render those marks, and `tests/legal-pages.test.ts`
pins that they do.

---

## Part 1 — missing facts (rendered as `[TO BE SUPPLIED: …]`)

### M1. FSSAI licence number for each outlet

- **Marked on:** `/legal/terms`
- **Token id:** `fssai-per-outlet`
- **Who supplies it:** Owner / Burgonomics team
- **Why it is needed:** Indian food law requires the licence of the kitchen that prepares the food to be displayed. There is one number per outlet, and the app already promises a per-store number on the menu and at checkout.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — fssaiLicense holds the masked 1072XXXXXXXXXX value, which the current terms page suppresses
- **Done when:** Every live outlet's real 14-digit FSSAI licence number is recorded (per outlet), printed on that outlet's menu/checkout legal surface, and the masked constant is gone.

### M2. Grievance Officer — full name

- **Marked on:** `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/grievance`
- **Token id:** `grievance-officer-name`
- **Who supplies it:** Owner
- **Why it is needed:** DPDP Act 2023 and IT Rules 2021 require a named individual, not a job title, to own a complaint.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — no officer name constant exists yet
- **Done when:** A named individual is appointed in writing and their full name renders on the grievance page instead of a mark.

### M3. Grievance Officer — phone number

- **Marked on:** `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/grievance`
- **Token id:** `grievance-officer-phone`
- **Who supplies it:** Owner
- **Why it is needed:** The grievance route needs a phone contact beside the mailbox, so a complaint cannot be blocked by a dead inbox.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — no officer phone constant exists yet
- **Done when:** A monitored phone number that reaches the named officer renders on the grievance page, and a test call from outside the organisation connects.

### M4. CIN, or a written confirmation that none applies

- **Marked on:** `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/terms`
- **Token id:** `cin`
- **Who supplies it:** Owner
- **Why it is needed:** The GST certificate names a partnership, so no CIN may apply — but that has never been confirmed in writing, and the field is currently empty.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — cin is an empty string
- **Done when:** Either the real CIN is in the constant and prints, or a written statement that the entity is a partnership with no CIN is on file and the page says exactly that.

## Part 2 — printed but unverified (no mark on the page, still blocking)

### C1. Registered address — printed today as: A-802, Unicus Shyamal, Shyamal Cross Road, Satellite, Ahmedabad, Gujarat 380015

- **Token id:** `registered-address-confirmation`
- **Who confirms it:** Owner
- **Why it is needed:** The address printed comes from an app constant, while the handover notes still describe a different one (a studio name), so it must be confirmed against the registration certificate.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — registeredAddress
- **Done when:** The owner confirms in writing that this exact address appears on the GST registration certificate (or supplies the correct one, which then replaces the constant).

### C2. GSTIN — printed today as: 24ABHFP6677N1ZG

- **Token id:** `gstin-confirmation`
- **Who confirms it:** Owner
- **Why it is needed:** This GSTIN prints on customer receipts and legal pages. The handover notes still describe the field as masked, so a wrong value would be a false tax disclosure on every invoice.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — gstin
- **Done when:** The owner confirms the exact 15-character GSTIN against the registration certificate, and a receipt printed from the app shows the same string.

### C3. Grievance / privacy mailbox — printed today as: privacy@burgonomics.com, nodal@burgonomics.com

- **Token id:** `grievance-mailbox`
- **Who confirms it:** Owner / Burgonomics team
- **Why it is needed:** A data-deletion or grievance request that quietly bounces is the exact failure the DPDP Act penalises. No evidence exists that any of these mailboxes is created.
- **Where it lands in code:** src/core/constants/app.ts — grievanceEmail, nodalEmail
- **Done when:** A test email sent from outside the organisation to both addresses is received and answered, and the fact is recorded with its date.

## What the release worker must do with this file

- Mirror both lists into the release checklist at
  `client-handover/STORE_SUBMISSION_CHECKLIST.md` (section "Legal facts — BLOCKING"). That section
  already exists; keep it in step.
- Do **not** submit either app to Google Play or the App Store while Part 1 is non-empty. A legal
  page carrying a visible placeholder is a rejection risk and, worse, an unenforceable disclosure.
- Do **not** treat Part 1 as engineering's job. The FSSAI licences, the Grievance Officer's name
  and phone, the CIN question and the mailbox confirmations all need the owner.

## How to verify the pages are clean

```bash
cd burgonomics-foundation-core
npm run legal:facts -- --check   # this file is in step with the content module
npm run legal:html               # regenerate the four published HTML pages
npm test -- tests/legal-pages.test.ts
```

Expected once every fact is in: `privacy 0  terms 0  refund-policy 0  grievance 0` missing
`[TO BE SUPPLIED:` marks, and no "not publishable yet" banner on any page.
